Consider adding an `anyOf` constraint per part requiring at least one of `{content|file_id|uri}` or `stripped_reason` to be present (allowing both if desired). Apply the same constraint to the corresponding part definitions in the system-instructions and output schemas.

threads.body: The `anyOf` here only checks that the *key* `content` or `stripped_reason` is present. Because `content` is nullable (`Optional[bytes]` with `default=None`), an instance like `{..., "content": null}` will satisfy the `{required:["content"]}` branch and validate even when `stripped_reason` is absent, which undermines the stated “payload vs stripped” distinction. Consider tightening the schema so the “payload present” branch requires a non-null value (e.g., constrain the branch’s `properties.content` to the non-null type / add `not: {type: "null"}`), and apply the same pattern to `file_id`/`uri`.

Having `content` optional on input but required on output/system instructions needs a parallel class hierarchy, union rewriting and shadowed class names just to keep `$defs` stable. I know it was asked for in https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/pull/144#discussion_r3327813684, but it doesn't make the PR easier to review. Output blobs hit the same capture limits, so how about making it optional on the shared `BlobPart` and regenerating all three schemas?

```python
class BlobPart(BaseModel):
    ...
    content: Optional[bytes] = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Raw bytes of the attached data. This field SHOULD be encoded as a base64 string when serialized to JSON. MAY be omitted when the instrumentation does not capture the payload inline.",
    )
```

Then this block goes away (and `output-messages-blob-missing-content.yaml` flips to a valid case):

```suggestion
class InputMessages(RootModel[List[ChatMessage]]):
```
